main_text.p: est, de jure teneatur. Id quod Ulpianus pronunciat de domino, qui passus est aliquem à servol.2.&3. occidi, cum eum prohi-bere potuisset.D. de Noxal. Action.

Manifestum id erat in servis qui erant de familiâ, qui nisi armis, etiam corporis objectu, cum possent, domino periclitanti auxilium tulerent[?], ultimo supplicio subjiciebantur.l.1.§.28. l.19. D. AdSena-tusc.Sila-nian.
Idem obtinuit in Vasallis, qui si Seniorem periclitantem in praelio deseruissent, feudo merito privabantur.c, unic.§. si quis miles,etc. de feud. fin. culp. nō amitt.

Neque obstat. 1. Quod Ulpianus ex Pomponio refert licere cuipiam ab alio pecuniam stipulari, & accipere hunc in finem, ut ipsum adversus hostium incursus tueatur. Unde inferri posse videtur, gratuito & ex officio neminem ad alterius defensionem esse obstrictum. Quod turpiter agere videretur,pecuniam accipiendo,

page.notes: The first word "eft" is printed with a long s and is transcribed as "est". Ink blots lie over the text on the right: near "domino" and "tulerent" (the word "tulerent" is partly covered, hence the [?]), and dark specks near "prohibere", "stipulari" and "turpiter" that are not printed marks and are not transcribed. The left margin notes are small and partly broken; their hyphenation is kept as printed. A faint digitiser's line sits at the bottom right and is omitted.
